answer: An agent marketplace requires every active identity, including agents named jade, zephyr, and mesa, to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting jobs. Creating accounts is cheap, but activating 10,000 fake agents ties up $1 million for a month. Closing an account does not release its bond early, so recycling identities cannot bypass the lock. The defense makes a sybil swarm costly in capital and lost interest.
